findings.note: Section 3.2 (spec lines 132-133) enumerates the prompt fixture layout and names `<kind>.plain.txt` files ("still-present.calibration.plain.txt and still-present.product.plain.txt") as the vendored copies of the Go constants. No .plain.txt file exists: internal/fsm/judge/testdata/prompts/ holds only <kind>.python.txt plus three golden modes per kind (.calibration.golden, .plain.golden, .fenced.golden). The provenance test compares rewrite(python.txt) against the in-code constant directly (internal/fsm/judge/judge_test.go:28 reads only *.python.txt), so no .plain.txt is needed - but the spec's file inventory describes a layout that was never built, and its own J1 row (line 308) lists only `.plain.golden`/`.fenced.golden`, omitting the third mode the test loop actually generates and asserts (judge_test.go:112 builds kind + "." + mode.name + ".golden" over all three modes).

findings.note: The `codex` provider - a third judge transport that spawns a local binary - is documented only as prose inside section 3.4 (spec lines 157-168) and is missing from every structural part of the spec that is meant to be the contract. The package summary line for judge (spec line 50) lists "providers; retry; tokens; MockJudge; NewHTTPClient" with no mention of it; the API sketch in section 3 (lines 88-103) declares New but not NewWithCodex or the CodexExec seam, both of which are shipped (internal/fsm/judge/judge.go:201, internal/fsm/judge/codex.go:24); none of the r3/r4/r5 revision notes in the status header (lines 3-12) record its addition; and the judge test table's rows J0-J9 (line 308) contain no codex row even though internal/fsm/judge/codex.go is under the 100%-coverage gate and has its own test file. The result is that the one judge path that executes a local process and reads an operator OAuth session under ~/.codex has no entry in the spec's test contract or freeze inventory - a reader auditing the trust boundary from the structural sections alone would not know it exists.

evidence.note: judge package inventory omits the codex provider.
CodexExec seam and the whole codex judge are shipped but absent from the spec's API sketch and test table.

findings.note: Undocumented calibration carve-out in the Anthropic family gate. Spec line 187 states flatly that "any other claude* id -> ERR_JUDGE_MODEL{reason: unknown_family}", and the J0 test row (line 308) repeats it as "unknown claude-zeta -> ERR_JUDGE_MODEL", with no mode qualifier. The shipped check is product-mode only: internal/fsm/judge/judge.go:290 reads `if capable, legacy := anthropicFamily(wireModel(model)); !calibration && !capable && !legacy`, so under --calibration an arbitrary or mistyped claude-* id passes Preflight and reaches the Anthropic API, failing there instead of locally. The behaviour is deliberate and pinned by a test ("unknown family under calibration is accepted", internal/fsm/judge/judge_test.go:766), which makes the spec the only thing that is wrong.

evidence.note: Unqualified claim that any other claude* id is refused with unknown_family.
!calibration && !capable && !legacy - the refusal is skipped entirely in calibration mode.

findings.note: Section 4.2's ordered list is numbered 1, 0, 2, 3 across spec lines 256, 262, 265 and 269, with the pre-flight step written as "0." and placed after the match loop. CommonMark takes the start number from the first item and renumbers the rest, so the rendered spec shows the cliff check as step 2, after the per-pair match calls - the exact opposite of its own text, "Pre-flight (before any call) ... with no spend". The implementation does run the bound first, so this is a rendering defect in the spec rather than in the code, but it inverts the one ordering guarantee the step exists to make.

evidence.note: List item written as "0. Pre-flight (before any call)" but positioned and rendered after item 1.
